turns.t: Hello, doctor. I'm sorry, this is rather embarrassing. I've been leaking urine. Mainly when I cough or sneeze, but also when I can't get to the toilet in time.
Please don't be embarrassed, it's very common, and very treatable. How long has this been happening?
Oh, I really couldn't say. It's crept up. A year? Two? I only noticed when I had to start wearing pads.
How often do you leak?
Most days. A few drops on a cough. And if I get the urge, I have to run, and sometimes I don't make it.
How often do you pass urine in a day, and at night?
Eight, nine times in the day. And twice at night.
Any burning, or blood in the urine? ~
No. None of that. ~
What tablets are you taking?
Furosemide, 40 mg, in the morning, for my ankles. A blood pressure tablet, I couldn't tell you the name, it's a little pink one. And a vitamin.
So the water tablet is 40 mg in the morning, and the pink blood-pressure tablet you can't name. What's the vitamin?
Vitamin D, I think, 800 units, once a day.
Thank you. Any other conditions?
High blood pressure, and I've had four children.
Do you drink a lot of tea or coffee, or take any fizzy drinks? ~
Four cups of tea in the morning, and I like a fizzy orange. ~
That could be adding to it. Let me ask a few more questions. Do you ever feel that your bladder hasn't emptied? ~
Sometimes. I'm up and down. ~
And any constipation? ~
Now and then. ~
I'd like to check your urine today with a dipstick, to rule out infection. ~
Fine. ~
I'd say what you describe, leaking on coughing and sneezing, and also an urgent need to go that you sometimes can't hold, is a mixture of stress and urge incontinence.
Two kinds? ~
It's very common to have both, especially after childbirth and with age. ~
What can be done? ~
First, pelvic floor exercises, squeezing the muscles you'd use to stop passing wind or urine, ten squeezes, three times a day.
I've heard of those. ~
They work for most people if done regularly for three months. I'll also refer you to the continence physiotherapist, who will teach you properly.
Right. ~
Cut down the tea, coffee and fizzy drinks, and don't drink too much in the evening. Keep a bladder diary for three days.
What do I write? ~
When you drink, what, how much, and when you pass urine, and any leaks. ~
I can do that. ~
I'd like to see you again in six weeks, with the diary.
Six weeks. Thank you. ~

symptoms.name: urge
symptoms.frequency: Eight, nine times in the day

clinical_assessment.assessment: a mixture of stress and urge incontinence

clinical_actions.description: Pelvic floor exercises ten squeezes three times a day
Cut tea, coffee and fizzy drinks, avoid evening fluids and keep a three-day bladder diary

clinical_uncertainties.description: Patient could not say when the leaking began ("A year? Two?").
Patient cannot name her blood pressure tablet and describes it as a little pink one.
